title: When the Veil Burns Again
premise: Odile Oyelaran, the last of the oath-bound swordspeakers, has spent fifteen years hiding in the Thornfell mountains, trading on smugglers' roads and burying the language that once bound blades to oaths. When a mute child arrives at their door speaking Thornic—the tongue of a kingdom erased from every map—Odile realizes the old country is not dead but sealed, and the child is its living key. Hunted by the Chancery's veil-burners and shadowed by a former comrade turned inquisitor, Odile must reforge their broken oath-sword and carry the child to the Door of Ash before the last solstice gate closes. In the end, Odile chooses love over duty: they send the child through to restore the lost country while remaining behind as its anchor in this one, becoming the bridge between two worlds at the cost of ever belonging wholly to either.
about_author: Elodie Sandoval is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. They write about borders, exile, and the languages people refuse to let die.

chapters.title: Salt on the Pass
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A routine smuggling run through the Thornfells establishes Odile's careful invisibility: no name spoken aloud, no blade drawn, no Thornic sung. The emotional beat is weary competence masking grief for a dead order.

chapters.title: The Child at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. On a storm night, a girl of perhaps eight appears at Odile's door, barefoot, unafraid, speaking fluent Thornic—a language Odile swore never to use again. The beat is terror disguised as irritation.

chapters.title: Words That Predate Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Testing the child's speech against half-remembered liturgies, Odile confirms she speaks pre-Imperial Thornic, older than the Veil that erased the country. Hope and dread arrive together.

chapters.title: What the Chancery Burns
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Maren Voss's POV. Voss, once Odile's shield-sister, arrives in the valley hunting 'linguistic contagion.' Her chapters reveal the Chancery's machinery—and her private doubt about what burning words actually buys.

chapters.title: The Oath-Sword in the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile digs up the shattered oath-sword buried beneath the hearth and finds it humming in response to the child's voice. The beat is reluctant reawakening.

chapters.title: A Name Is a Debt
chapters.summary: The child's POV, rendered in close third. She remembers fragments of a country Odile thought was gone: green terraces, bell-towers, a door. She cannot say how she crossed over.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Logic
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile plans an escape route using old smuggler roads, but every path runs through Chancery checkpoints. An old fence named Brannick offers a dangerous favor. Beat: pragmatism strained by protectiveness.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Voss interrogates villagers and finds a child's bootprint near Odile's cabin. Flashbacks show her and Odile swearing the final oath as the Veil fell. Beat: loyalty splitting down the middle.

chapters.title: The Bell That Still Rings
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Following the child's memories, Odile and she find a drowned bell in a high tarn that rings only in Thornic. Its tolling marks them on every Chancery resonance-map. Beat: wonder curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: Burned Road
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Chancery veil-burners torch the eastern passes; Brannick dies covering their escape. Odile draws the reforged sword for the first time in fifteen years and speaks one word of Thornic. Beat: the cost of survival made visible.

chapters.title: What I Swore at Ashfall
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Voss reconstructs the fall of the old country and learns the Veil wasn't protection—it was imprisonment, sealing a whole nation out of existence. Beat: faith cracking.

chapters.title: The Child Teaches the Sword
chapters.summary: The child's POV. Hiding in a cave shrine, she teaches Odile the true forms of the oath-words; the sword drinks them like rain. Their bond deepens into something like family. Beat: tenderness under threat.

chapters.title: Sister Against Sister
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Voss corners them at the shrine. Blades cross; neither can land a killing stroke. Voss lets them go—but reports a false position, buying time she may pay for with her life. Beat: love against duty, embodied.

chapters.title: The Map No One Drew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The child's memories and Odile's smuggler knowledge combine to locate the Door of Ash beneath a glacier, reachable only before solstice. Beat: grim resolve.

chapters.title: Cold Country
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The glacier crossing: whiteout, crevasse, frostbite, and the sword singing louder as they near the door. Odile begins to understand what passage will demand. Beat: endurance.

chapters.title: The Price Written Twice
chapters.summary: The child's POV. At the threshold carvings, the terms appear: one may pass freely; the one who opens must remain as anchor, bound between worlds forever. The child tries to claim the role herself. Beat: heartbreak.

chapters.title: Veil-Burners at the Ice
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Voss's superiors, suspicious of her false report, dispatch a full company. Voss defects openly, racing to warn Odile. Beat: treason as conscience.

chapters.title: When the Veil Burns Again
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Climax: battle on the ice before the Door. Odile speaks the full oath, the sword blazing, while the child sings the country back into being beyond the threshold. Voss holds the line beside them. Beat: fury transfigured into ceremony.

chapters.title: The Choosing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With the door open and the company broken, Odile takes the anchor's burden from the child, sending her through to the restored country. Beat: sacrifice chosen freely, love outweighing duty.

chapters.title: Between Two Doors
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Bound as anchor, Odile experiences both worlds at once—the restored Thornic kingdom flickering through the ice like light through water. Voss stays as witness and protector. Beat: awe laced with loneliness.

chapters.title: Letters in a Living Tongue
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Seasons pass. The child, now thriving in the old country, sends messages through the door; Odile answers in Thornic, teaching scattered survivors the words again. Beat: quiet repair.

chapters.title: The Door Stands Open
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Odile's POV. On the next solstice, the Door widens enough for pilgrims to pass both ways. Odile, still anchored, greets the first travelers home. The beat is bittersweet peace: invisible no longer, belonging everywhere and nowhere, and content.
